deep.reconstruction:
Setting (continued from p.30). Grothendieck has a combinatorial graph Γ=(S, A⃗, σ0, σ), where A⃗ is the set of oriented edges and a⃗ ↦ −a⃗ (also written a⃖) is reversal. At each vertex s he fixes a polygonal (dihedral) structure on the star A⃗_s of edges with origin s. He writes ω_s=ω(A⃗_s) for its two-element set of orientations. For each a⃗: s→t he gives a 'transport isomorphism' φ_a⃗: ω_s → ω_t, subject only to φ_{−a⃗}=φ_a⃗^{-1}. In modern terms this is a Z/2-local system of orientations on Γ. Up to gauge it is the same as a signed (twisted) rotation system, i.e. the data of a possibly non-orientable map. On p.30 the surface is built by taking for each vertex s the polygonal disc Dis_s dual to A⃗_s and gluing sides α_a⃗ and α_{−a⃗} by affine maps. The gluing must reverse the orientations that correspond under φ_a⃗.

This page:
(1) Gluing gives a compact connected topological surface. The cell subdivision of |Γ| defined by Γ is embedded in it.
(2) Faces. Let Rep be the set of pairs (a⃗, ω) with ω an orientation at s=or(a⃗); these are the 'repères' or flags, and |Rep| = Σ 2ν_s = 4|E|. Define ρ_f(a⃗, ω_s) = (b⃗, ω_t), where ω_t = φ_a⃗(ω_s) and b⃗ = ρ_{ω_t}^{-1}(−a⃗). Here ρ_ω is the cyclic permutation of A⃗_t given by ω. Oriented faces correspond to ρ_f-orbits. This is the face-tracing algorithm for twisted rotation systems, and it is the rotation of the dual map C*.
(3) Flag (cartographic) description of the map C = (Γ, (ω_s), (φ_a⃗)). There are three involutions on Rep, functorial in the A⃗_s:
  - σ0(a⃗, ω_s) = (−a⃗, −φ_a⃗ ω_s): changes the vertex, keeps edge and face.
  - σ2(a⃗, ω_s) = (a⃗, −ω_s): changes the face.
  - σ1(a⃗, ω_s) = (ρ_{ω_s}(a⃗), −ω_s): changes the edge.
  Equivalently, Rep(C) ≅ ⊔_s Rep(A⃗_s), the disjoint union of the flag sets of the vertex polygons. Then σ1 and σ2 become the usual polygon flag involutions σ̃0 and σ̃1, which change the polygon's vertex and side respectively; dimensions shift by one under duality. σ0 is the only operation coupling different vertices, through φ.
(4) Rotations:
  - ρ_som = σ2σ1 gives (ρ_ω(a⃗), ω), the rotation around a vertex.
  - ρ_face = σ1σ0. One checks σ1σ0(a⃗, ω) = (ρ_{−φω}(−a⃗), φω) = (ρ_{φω}^{-1}(−a⃗), φω), which is exactly ρ_f above.
  - σ := σ2σ0 gives (−a⃗, φ_a⃗ ω), the fixed-point-free edge involution lifting a⃗ ↦ −a⃗ to Rep.

Purpose. In the pseudo-line project, arrangements live on the projective plane, which is non-orientable. Grothendieck therefore needs a flag/cartographic model of non-orientable maps built from graph-plus-local-orientation data. This connects the arrangement combinatorics to the σ0, σ1, σ2 formalism of the Esquisse.
errors: The last line labels σ2σ0 as ρ_f ('ρ_f = σ2σ0 =def σ'). σ2σ0 is not the face rotation: it is the edge involution (a⃗, ω) ↦ (−a⃗, φω), which changes vertex and face but keeps the edge. The face rotation, matching the earlier definition of ρ_f, is σ1σ0, as he correctly writes just above ('ρ_face = σ1σ0'). Most likely σ is simply being defined as the lift of the edge-reversal involution, and the ρ_f label is a slip or a crossed-out remnant.

Minor: ρ_som = σ2σ1 is written as σ̃0^s σ̃1^s. With σ1 = σ̃0 and σ2 = σ̃1 it should be σ̃1σ̃0. Since these are involutions, this only changes the rotation to its inverse, a matter of orientation convention.

Hypotheses are left implicit. Connectedness of the surface needs Γ connected. Vertices of order 1 or 2 require the extra conventions mentioned on p.30. The formula for σ1 assumes ρ_{−ω} = ρ_ω^{-1}, which is true.

ideas.what: Non-orientable map encoded as graph + dihedral (polygon) structure at each vertex + transport isomorphisms φ_a between vertex orientation torsors, with φ_{-a}=φ_a^{-1}; the surface is obtained by gluing dual polygons
ideas.modern_name: signed/twisted rotation system (generalized embedding scheme), stated gauge-invariantly as a Z/2 orientation local system on the graph
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ringel; Stahl (generalized embedding schemes, 1978); Gross–Tucker, Topological Graph Theory (1987)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) treats maps and the cartographic group, but I do not know of this torsor-transport formulation there

ideas.what: Faces = orbits of ρ_f(a,ω)=(ρ_{φ_a ω}^{-1}(−a), φ_a ω) on flags
ideas.usually_credited_to: Heffter/Edmonds for orientable; Ringel, Stahl for non-orientable

ideas.what: Map as a set of flags with three involutions σ0,σ1,σ2 (σ0σ2 an involution); Rep(C)=⊔ Rep(A_s); ρ_som=σ2σ1, ρ_face=σ1σ0
ideas.modern_name: cartographic group / flag-system (gem) description of maps
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984), section on cartographic groups C2 and maps (cartes)

missed.claim: Grothendieck presents the twist data of a non-orientable map as a Z/2-torsor with 'connection' (transport isomorphisms between the two-element orientation sets of vertex stars), rather than as edge signs. The gauge (switching) equivalence is thereby built in, and the cartographic involutions come out functorial in the vertex stars. This is a clean viewpoint but mathematically equivalent to known signed rotation systems. Its use here is to bridge pseudo-line arrangements on RP^2 to the Esquisse flag formalism.
missed.quote: il faut expliciter les opérations fonctorielles en A⃗_s σ0,σ1,σ2 sur Rep
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Minor: documents how Grothendieck adapted the cartographic-group formalism to non-orientable maps in the pseudo-line project. That is of historical interest, not a new result.

deep.surprise_reason: Correct but standard: a flag/cartographic-group description of non-orientable maps from twisted rotation systems, all known (Tutte, Lins, Stahl, Bryant–Singerman). The only distinctive features are the gauge-invariant torsor formulation and its role in the pseudo-line project. There is also a small labeling slip (σ2σ0 called ρ_f).
transcription_corrections: Bottom line: read as '[ρ_face struck] ρ_f = σ2σ0 =def σ' preceded by a struck/abbreviated word. In context σ2σ0 is the edge involution; the face rotation appears correctly in the line above as 'ρ_face = σ1σ0'.
'Rep 𝓔' near the top right should probably read 'Rep C' (the flag set of the map C), consistent with the later 'Rep(C) ≃ ⊔_{s∈S} Rep(A⃗_s)'.
The marginal note under Rep(A⃗_s) appears to read 'ens. des drapeaux (orientés?) a⃗' with a crossed-out word; it glosses Rep(A⃗_s) as the set of flags.

In 'C est aussi l'opération de rotation sur le ... de la carte duale C*', the struck words seem to be 'C est aussi', replaced by 'C'est aussi l'opération de rotation sur les [sommets] de la carte duale C*'.
